title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
quote: In practice, we find that the block size 16 is large enough to efficiently utilize the GPU and small enough to avoid significant internal fragmentation in most workloads. Accordingly, vLLM sets its default block size as 16.
proves: Changes KV storage to fixed-size non-contiguous blocks. Block size 16 chosen from a sweep on 2 traces only (ShareGPT: 16-128 best; Alpaca: 16-32 best, larger degrades). Paged kernel costs 20-26% higher attention kernel latency vs FasterTransformer.
does_not_prove: Block size studied only on A100-class GPUs, OPT/LLaMA fp16, 2 traces, with 2023 kernels; never revisited for prefix-cache hit rate, unified memory, or quantized KV. No limitations section in abstract.
bearing: supports: block-size tradeoff gap on unified-memory/4-bit setups; threatens: naive block-size sweep on GPU (already done once)

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention (eviction and recovery)
quote: we implement an all-or-nothing eviction policy, i.e., either evict all or none of the blocks of a sequence.
proves: Preemption is fixed by design: all-or-nothing per sequence, FCFS scheduling. Swap vs recompute studied vs block size: swap bad at small blocks (PCIe small transfers), recompute overhead never above 20% of swap latency; comparable at 16-64.
does_not_prove: Partial (per-block) eviction and non-FCFS victim choice not studied. Swap/recompute tradeoff measured over PCIe only; on unified memory there is no PCIe copy, so the tradeoff is unmeasured there.
bearing: supports: partial-sequence preemption, swap-vs-recompute on unified memory; threatens: none directly

title: Mooncake: A KVCache-centric Disaggregated Architecture for LLM Serving
quote: LRUCache performs best under this dataset's patterns, likely due to the temporal proximity in request utilization.
proves: Changes where KV lives: disaggregated prefill/decode with a distributed KV pool. Hash block size 512 tokens. Eviction compared on Kimi trace: LRU 0.46 vs LFU 0.40 vs LengthAware 0.40 hit rate at 10k blocks; all converge to 0.55 at infinite capacity. Request-level output-length prediction left to future work.
does_not_prove: Eviction comparison is hit rate only (not TTFT or recompute cost), one trace, 3 simple policies; 512-token hash block not studied; evaluated with a dummy LLaMA2-70B.
bearing: threatens: simple LFU/length-aware eviction beating LRU on chat traces; supports: cost-aware eviction gap, prefix-block granularity gap

title: Mooncake: Trading More Storage for Less Computation - A KVCache-centric Architecture for Serving LLM Chatbot
quote: Mooncake is the serving platform for Kimi, an LLM chatbot service developed by Moonshot AI.
proves: Confirms Mooncake appeared at USENIX FAST 25 as a production system for Kimi.
does_not_prove: Venue page only; technical details taken from arXiv row A3.
bearing: context: venue confirmation for A3

title: Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving
quote: the downtime of migration is nearly constant with increasing sequence lengths (roughly 20-30 ms)
proves: Changes KV movement: live migration of a request's KV across instances using multi-stage copy that relies on KV being append-only. Load metric freeness F=(M-sum V)/B with virtual usage. High-priority headroom 1,600 tokens chosen empirically without sweep; migration thresholds unstated.
does_not_prove: Migration thresholds and headroom never swept; evaluated on vLLM with LLaMA max 2k sequence; single-model-type. Future work: interplay of global scheduling with local scheduling.
bearing: supports: intra-instance analogs (e.g. headroom reservation, virtual-usage admission) on single device; threatens: cross-instance migration ideas (not doable on one laptop anyway)

title: Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving (venue page)
quote: live migration mechanism for requests and their in-memory states
proves: Confirms OSDI 24 publication and the live-migration framing.
does_not_prove: Venue page only.
bearing: context: venue confirmation for A5

title: RetrievalAttention: Accelerating Long-Context LLM Inference via Vector Retrieval
quote: The size of the static pattern is consistently 640 (128 initial tokens + 512 tokens in the local window)
proves: Changes KV placement and access: ANN index over KV vectors in CPU memory, attention-aware search for OOD queries; accesses 1-3% of data; 128K context on RTX 4090 at 0.188 s/token. Static GPU pattern fixed at 640 tokens and top-k 100 without ablation.
does_not_prove: Single-batch only; assumes prefill done in advance; index build time not analyzed; static window size and top-k not swept; one index per query head (GQA cost).
bearing: supports: static-window size / top-k sensitivity gap, index-build cost gap; threatens: generic retrieval-based sparse attention novelty

title: FlexiCache: Leveraging Temporal Stability of Attention Heads for Efficient KV Cache Management
quote: We classify the least stable 25% of heads as unstable and the remaining heads as stable.
proves: FlexiCache is a vLLM-based per-head KV offload system: unstable heads keep all pages on GPU, stable heads keep top-K pages (64 pages of 16 tokens) and offload the rest to host; rerank every 16 steps. Up to 70% GPU memory reduction, 1.38-1.55x offline throughput.
does_not_prove: 25% split, page size 16 and rerank interval 16 are fixed without sweep; only token budget (1024/2048) varied. Assumes two-level GPU-CPU hierarchy; multi-node transfer open.
bearing: supports: rerank-interval and stable-head-fraction sensitivity gap; threatens: per-head offload as a new idea

title: FlexiCache (MLSys proceedings page)
quote: reduces GPU memory footprint for long-context requests by up to 70%
proves: Confirms FlexiCache is in Proceedings of Machine Learning and Systems 8 (MLSys 2026).
does_not_prove: Venue page only.
bearing: context: venue confirmation for A8

title: Strata: Hierarchical Context Caching for Long Context Language Model Serving
quote: a default threshold of 100 active token matches proved effective
proves: Strata is an SGLang-based GPU/CPU/SSD hierarchical KV cache: GPU-assisted I/O decouples GPU and host layouts (up to 4x lower disk-load latency), delay-hit deferral, balanced batching, bubble filling. Up to 5x lower TTFT vs vLLM+LMCache. Page size 1, delay-hit threshold 100, loading-bound ratio 100 all fixed without sweep.
does_not_prove: No eviction policy named or studied; thresholds not swept; single-instance only; disk tier unused in many benchmarks.
bearing: supports: delay-hit threshold sensitivity, eviction policy in tiered cache gap; threatens: layout-decoupling and loading-aware scheduling as new ideas

title: Strata (OSDI 26 page)
quote: We present Strata, a hierarchical context caching framework for long-context LLM serving.
proves: Confirms Strata at 20th USENIX OSDI 26.
does_not_prove: Venue page only.
bearing: context: venue confirmation for A10

title: vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention
quote: We find that the choice of page size does not affect vAttention as long as fragmentation is not a concern.
proves: Changes KV allocation: contiguous virtual KV with demand-mapped physical pages via CUDA VMM. Paged prefill kernels up to 37%/42% slower; block-table prep was 30% of decode latency in vLLM; up to 1.23x throughput. Page size studied (64KB-2MB).
does_not_prove: CUDA-specific; decode throughput only matches PagedAttention; swap to CPU left as future work. Not tested on unified memory where VMM semantics differ.
bearing: threatens: claims that paging cost dominates; supports: measuring block-table/paging overhead on Metal

title: vLLM design doc: prefix_caching (title not recorded)
quote: We only cache full blocks.
proves: vLLM prefix cache: LRU free-queue eviction; blocks of a finished request are freed in reverse so the last block is evicted first, because it hashes more tokens and is less likely reused; only full blocks are hashed.
does_not_prove: No measurement of hit rate or cost; partial-block caching and cost-aware eviction not evaluated.
bearing: supports: partial-block prefix caching gap, cost-aware eviction in vLLM; threatens: nothing

title: LMSYS blog post on SGLang, 2024-01-17 (title not recorded)
quote: We implement a Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policy, complemented by a cache-aware scheduling policy
proves: RadixAttention keeps prompt and generation KV in a radix tree, LRU leaf eviction, cache-aware (longest-prefix-first) scheduling.
does_not_prove: LRU chosen by default, no policy comparison in blog.
bearing: threatens: radix/prefix sharing as new idea; supports: eviction-policy gap on radix trees

title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
quote: novel optimizations like RadixAttention for KV cache reuse
proves: SGLang paper reports up to 6.4x throughput with RadixAttention among other optimizations.
does_not_prove: Abstract page only; venue (NeurIPS 2024) not shown on page.
bearing: context for A14

title: HiCache design (SGLang docs)
quote: Uses hit-count tracking to back up only frequently accessed data
proves: HiCache extends radix tree across GPU/host/storage tiers with selectable write policies (write_through, write_through_selective, write_back), prefetch policies, prefetch threshold 256 tokens, layouts layer_first (GPU default) / page_first.
does_not_prove: Docs give no data on which write policy or layout wins under which workload.
bearing: supports: tier write-policy comparison study (exposed knob, unstudied); threatens: building tiered cache from scratch

title: KVCache Cache in the Wild: Characterizing and Optimizing KVCache Cache at a Large Cloud Provider
quote: 10 % of KV$ blocks contribute to 77 % of the reuses.
proves: Alibaba trace study: single-turn requests are 97% of hits in to-B trace; 80% of reuse within 10 min (Trace A) or 10 s (Trace B); workload-aware eviction beats LRU/FIFO/LFU/S3-FIFO by 8.1-23.9% hit rate but only 1.5-3.9% over the best baseline; up to 41.4% mean response time gain vs LRU.
does_not_prove: Single-instance eviction only; on Trace B policy falls back to LRU; reasoning workloads not covered.
bearing: threatens: eviction-policy tweaks (small gain over best baseline); supports: reasoning/agent workload KV reuse gap

title: Jenga: Effective Memory Management for Serving LLM with Heterogeneity
quote: employs a two-level memory allocator, leveraging the least common multiple (LCM) of embedding sizes
proves: Changes KV allocation for heterogeneous layers (sliding window, Mamba, cross-attention, spec decode): up to 79.6% better memory utilization, up to 4.92x throughput on vLLM.
does_not_prove: SOSP venue not confirmed on opened page. Targets heterogeneous models; not studied on Apple silicon.
bearing: threatens: hybrid-model KV allocator ideas; supports: per-layer-type eviction policy study

title: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
quote: typically evict KV caches using a Least Recently Used (LRU) policy, which fails to anticipate future agent usage and often discards KV caches shortly before their reuse.
proves: Replaces LRU with steps-to-execution eviction from an Agent Step Graph plus CPU-to-GPU prefetch; up to 1.83x (single workflow) and 2.19x (many workflows) vs SGLang hierarchical radix cache.
does_not_prove: Needs workflow graph known in advance; not general chat.
bearing: threatens: future-aware eviction for agents; supports: eviction without workflow hints gap

title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
quote: selectively recomputes the KV values of a small subset of tokens
proves: Changes KV reuse to non-prefix chunks with selective recompute; TTFT 2.2-3.3x lower and throughput 2.8-5x higher vs full recompute.
does_not_prove: Venue not shown on page; recompute fraction knob and quality limits not covered by abstract.
bearing: threatens: non-prefix KV reuse as new idea; supports: recompute-fraction sensitivity study

title: LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference
quote: extracts and stores KV caches generated by modern LLM engines (vLLM and SGLang) out of the GPU memory
proves: KV offload/sharing layer across engines and queries; up to 15x throughput on multi-round QA and document analysis. Default chunk size 256 (per A10).
does_not_prove: Chunk size choice not studied in opened text.
bearing: threatens: KV offload layer as new idea; supports: chunk-size granularity gap

title: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
quote: can be speculated by performing a minimal rehearsal
proves: Prefetches only important KV from host using a rehearsal with partial next-layer query weights and key cache; up to 3.00x over prior offloading systems.
does_not_prove: Offloading over PCIe; unified memory removes the transfer that InfiniGen hides.
bearing: threatens: speculative KV prefetch novelty; supports: re-evaluating offload ideas on unified memory

title: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
quote: DistServe assigns prefill and decoding computation to different GPUs, hence eliminating prefill-decoding interferences.
proves: Prefill/decode disaggregation placed by cluster bandwidth; 7.4x more requests or 12.6x tighter SLO.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not discuss KV transfer cost; multi-GPU only.
bearing: low relevance on one laptop; context for KV transfer line

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
quote: novel admission and eviction policies that more judiciously assess potential cache entries
proves: Prefix cache for hybrid attention+SSM models with admission and FLOP-efficiency-aware eviction; up to 34.4x higher token hit rate, 617 ms lower TTFT.
does_not_prove: Hybrid models only; the FLOP-per-byte eviction idea not tested on pure-attention models.
bearing: threatens: cost-aware (FLOP-saved per byte) eviction novelty; supports: porting that score to pure transformers

title: kvcached
quote: it enables elastic and demand-driven KV cache allocation, improving GPU utilization under dynamic workloads.
proves: Virtual-memory elastic KV allocation library integrated with SGLang and vLLM (tested up to vLLM v0.30.0), for GPUs shared between workloads.
does_not_prove: No paper numbers opened; CUDA-only.
bearing: threatens: elastic KV pool idea on GPU; supports: elastic KV sizing on unified memory (shared with OS)

title: RetroInfer: A Vector Storage Engine for Scalable Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: a vector storage engine that realizes a sparsity-based KV cache for long-context inference
proves: RetrievalAttention successor: clustered wave index with GPU centroids plus wave buffer; up to 4.4x decode throughput vs full attention at 120K, 12.2x over sparse baselines at 1M tokens.
does_not_prove: Numbers changed across versions; targets GPU+CPU split.
bearing: threatens: retrieval/cluster-based KV index novelty

title: ShadowKV: KV Cache in Shadows for High-Throughput Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: stores the low-rank key cache and offloads the value cache
proves: Low-rank keys on GPU, values offloaded, sparse KV reconstructed on the fly; up to 6x batch, 3.04x throughput on A100.
does_not_prove: Venue not shown; offload benefit depends on discrete GPU memory.
bearing: threatens: low-rank key + offload novelty

title: KunServe: Parameter-centric Memory Management for Efficient Memory Overloading Handling in LLM Serving
quote: Prior KVCache-centric approaches handle overloading by dropping, migrating, or swapping KVCache.
proves: Llumnix follow-up: under overload, drop replicated parameters instead of KV; up to 72.2x lower tail TTFT vs Llumnix, vLLM, InferCept.
does_not_prove: Needs multiple GPUs with parameter replicas.
bearing: threatens: KV-only overload handling as complete; low direct relevance to one device

title: KVCache Cache in the Wild: Characterizing and Optimizing KVCache Cache at a Large Cloud Provider
quote: In Trace A, 80% of the reuse time falls within less than 10 minutes, while in Trace B it falls within 10 seconds.
proves: Alibaba Bailian (Qwen) production study: reuse is skewed (19% of user requests in trace A, 4% in B give >90% of block hits); single-turn requests give 97% of hits in API trace B; ideal infinite-cache hit rates 62%/54%; capacity of about 2x per-GPU HBM approaches ideal hit rate; workload-aware (WA) eviction gets 1.5-3.9% higher hit rate than best baseline and up to 41.4% mean response time gain vs LRU/LFU.
does_not_prove: Hit-rate gain over the best baseline is only a few points; no isolated LRU hit-rate number in text; datacenter scale and large models, not single-device; full trace not released (only a 2-hour sample, see B21).
bearing: supports: reuse is predictable per workload type; threatens: big hit-rate wins from fancier eviction (gain over best baseline is 1.5-3.9 pts)

title: When Fancy Eviction Fails: Rethinking Cache Replacement For LLM Prefix Reuse
quote: LRU is within 0.4 points of the best online algorithm on every trace
proves: 14 eviction algorithms (recency, frequency, learned) on two production traces (FreeInference 10.5B tokens, agent-heavy; Chutes 9.7B tokens) give little benefit over LRU because session pacing makes recency predictive; at 24 GiB on Qwen To-B trace S3-FIFO 0.491 vs LRU 0.403 hit ratio; by 1 TiB LRU within 0.4 pts of best; 84.9% of single-turn prompt blocks are accessed exactly once; block-level beats session-level eviction in HBM regime (session-level costs LRU 10.5 pts at 24 GiB); compute-aware partial-node eviction in vLLM cut TTFT 19.9% at 48 GiB; large gap to Belady remains.
does_not_prove: Datacenter GPU capacities (24 GiB+), not small unified memory; traces and simulator promised but not yet released; the small-capacity S3-FIFO win and compute-aware win are the open edges, not settled.
bearing: threatens: generic fancy eviction at large capacity; supports: one-hit quick demotion / admission and compute-aware partial eviction at small capacity (Mac 16 GB is exactly the small-capacity regime)

title: Learned Prefix Caching for Efficient LLM Inference (LPC)
quote: LPC achieves 18-47% reductions in required cache sizes for equivalent hit ratios
proves: Learned eviction that predicts from conversation content whether a conversation will continue, combined with last-access time, shrinks cache size needed for the same hit ratio by 18-47% on three real datasets; 11% prefill throughput gain.
does_not_prove: Throughput gain only in an emulated environment; abstract only (full paper not opened); predictor cost on-device not measured here.
bearing: threatens: learned/content-aware eviction as novel; supports: small-cache regime matters

title: Tail-Optimized Caching for LLM Inference
quote: achieves up to 27.5% reduction in P90 tail Time to First Token latency
proves: LRU ignores conversation length and can be arbitrarily bad for tail latency; Tail-Optimized LRU (small modification, provably optimal under a stochastic conversation model) cuts P90 TTFT up to 27.5%, P95 23.9%, SLO violations at 200 ms up to 38.9% on WildChat. Now shipped in SGLang as tlru (see B6).
does_not_prove: Simulated/stochastic-model evaluation on one dataset; mean TTFT effect not the target.
bearing: threatens: tail-aware eviction (already in SGLang); supports: measuring it on vLLM where it is absent

title: Not All Tokens Are Worth Caching: Learning Semantic-Aware Eviction for LLM Prefix Caches (SAECache)
quote: up to 756x variation in reuse rates
proves: Reuse rate differs by up to 756x across token types (system prompt, user query, chain-of-thought); multi-queue eviction with online-learned token weights gives 1.4x-2.7x TTFT over production-style baselines; fixed-parameter variants degrade up to 2.7x under workload mismatch.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; which baselines and capacities unclear; no single-device result.
bearing: threatens: token-type-aware eviction (e.g. evict thinking tokens first) as novel; supports: reasoning-token eviction gap on small devices

title: SGLang docs: Radix eviction policy
quote: The prefix unused for longest.
proves: SGLang exposes --radix-eviction-policy with lru (default), lfu, slru (protected_threshold, default 2), priority, tlru (threshold, next_prompt_estimate); fifo/mru/filo exist only for experiments; ties fall back to LRU; policy only ranks evictable leaves, cannot pin KV; docs advise starting with lru and changing only against measured hit rate.
does_not_prove: Docs give no benchmark numbers for any policy; no admission control knob in the radix cache itself.
bearing: supports: SGLang is a ready testbed for policy comparison; threatens: claiming SLRU/LFU/TLRU are untested ideas (they are shipped)

title: vLLM docs: Prefix caching design
quote: We only cache full blocks.
proves: vLLM evicts from the head of a free queue (LRU over ref-count-0 blocks); a freed request's blocks enter in reverse order so its last block, which hashes more tokens and is less likely reused, is evicted first; block hash chains parent hash + tokens + extras (LoRA, mm, cache salt); default hash sha256 since v0.11, options sha256_cbor, xxhash, xxhash_cbor.
does_not_prove: No eviction-policy alternative is offered or measured; docs give no hit-rate data.
bearing: supports: vLLM eviction is a fixed LRU with no knob, so any policy change is a code change worth measuring

title: vLLM API docs: CacheConfig
quote: The finest token boundary (in tokens) a prefix-cache hit can land on.
proves: Current vLLM CacheConfig has enable_prefix_caching (default True), prefix_caching_hash_algo (default sha256), block_size (default 16), prefix_match_unit, derived hash_block_size and cache_hit_alignment_tokens (hits can land finer than scheduler block size), prefix_cache_retention_interval for sliding-window/Mamba checkpoints; no field selects an eviction policy.
does_not_prove: Fetched latest docs, not the 0.31.0 pin; whether prefix_match_unit is honored by vllm-metal is unknown; no measured effect of match granularity.
bearing: supports: match-granularity (hash block size vs scheduler block size) tradeoff is a new, unmeasured knob; supports: eviction-policy gap in vLLM

title: Avoiding hash collisions in prefix cache (vLLM forum thread)
quote: Looks like `hashlib.blake2b` + `orjson` is the fastest safe solution.
proves: For 50k tokens (3,125 blocks): Python hash() 0.34 ms vs sha256 2.0 ms without serialization; serialization dominates (sha256+pickle 4.0 ms, +json 10.3 ms); on Apple M2 sha256+pickle 3.58 ms vs hash 0.68 ms; led to PR #15297 switching to sha256.
does_not_prove: Microbenchmarks only; end-to-end results shown only as images; per-request cost relative to prefill on a Mac not measured; xxhash excluded from that test.
bearing: supports: hash cost vs prefill time on slow-prefill devices is a small, measurable question; threatens: claiming hashing is a bottleneck on GPUs

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
quote: Marconi uses the second occurrence to identify the prefix and checkpoint its states.
proves: Hybrid (SSM+attention) models cannot roll back in-place SSM states, so naive prefix caching thrashes; Marconi admits only reuse-likely prefixes (second-occurrence or end-of-round states) and evicts by FLOP savings per byte plus recency; up to 34.4x higher token hit rate vs vLLM+ (avg 4.5x/7.3x/34.4x on LMSys/ShareGPT/SWEBench), 71.1% / 617 ms lower TTFT.
does_not_prove: Hybrid models only; for pure-attention Qwen3 the admission rule is untested; baselines are authors' extended vLLM+/SGLang+.
bearing: supports: admission (second-hit) and FLOP-aware eviction exist only for hybrids; gap: second-hit admission for pure-attention KV at small capacity

title: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
quote: the LRU policy identifies the Expresser's KV cache as the eviction candidate since it has not been accessed recently.
proves: In multi-agent workflows LRU evicts the next agent's prefix just before use; KVFlow evicts by steps-to-execution from the workflow graph plus overlapped CPU prefetch; up to 1.83x (single workflow, large prompts) and 2.19x (many concurrent workflows) over SGLang with HiCache.
does_not_prove: No ablation separating eviction from prefetching; needs workflow graph known in advance.
bearing: threatens: workflow-aware eviction; supports: isolating eviction-only effect is an open small experiment

title: Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live
quote: improves the average job completion times by over 8x
proves: Pinning a tool-calling request's KV in GPU memory with a TTL chosen from reload cost and ordering benefit cuts average agent job completion time by over 8x across three agent benchmarks and 8B-355B models.
does_not_prove: TTL tuned for datacenter GPUs; effect when memory is tiny and pins compete with batch is not covered on the page I read.
bearing: threatens: TTL/pinning for agent tool pauses

title: CacheWise: Understanding Workloads and Optimizing KVCache Management for Efficiently Serving LLM Coding Agents
quote: CacheWise reduces KVCache evictions by up to 2-2.6x and improves total agent session completion time by up to 3.5x.
proves: Coding-agent workload study plus predictive eviction using tool-duration estimates cuts evictions 2-2.6x and session completion time up to 3.5x vs conventional serving policies.
does_not_prove: Baselines not named in abstract; workload numbers not in abstract.
bearing: threatens: tool-duration-aware eviction for coding agents

title: PEEK: Predictive Queue-Informed KV Cache Management for LLM Serving
quote: PEEK delivers up to 3.0×/2.6× cache hit, 7.9×/7.1× TTFT, 6.7×/5.5× E2E, and 3.6×/4.5× throughput gains
proves: Eviction that looks at the waiting queue (protect prefixes pending requests need) gives up to 3.0x/2.6x cache hit and 7.9x/7.1x TTFT over best stock SGLang/vLLM baselines.
does_not_prove: Gains are vs stock engines under queueing load; small-batch single-user setting unclear.
bearing: threatens: queue-aware eviction (protect what waiting requests need)

title: Leyline: KV Cache Directives for Agentic Inference
quote: The splice kernel lifts replay cache-hit by +11.2 pp and cuts latency by up to 241 ms.
proves: An interface letting agents issue KV cache directives (e.g. splice, truncation) lifts replay cache hit by 11.2 pp and agentic solve rate by 14.3 pp; per search snippet, it notes a vLLM RFC for pluggable non-LRU eviction ended without an accepted abstraction.
does_not_prove: Pluggable-eviction RFC status is second-hand (from search snippet, not the issue).
bearing: threatens: app-hinted cache directives; supports: vLLM lacks a pluggable eviction API

title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
quote: the cache hit rate ranges from 50% to 99%
proves: RadixAttention: token-level radix tree with LRU leaf eviction; cache-aware scheduling sorts waiting requests by matched prefix length; Theorem 3.1 says DFS order of the radix tree is optimal offline (cache >= max request length); scheduling reaches about 96% of optimal hit rate on average.
does_not_prove: Optimality only for offline batches; benchmarks are structured programs with heavy sharing, not production traces.
bearing: supports: token-level radix vs block hash is a design axis; threatens: cache-aware batch ordering as novel

title: Requests of a Feather Must Flock Together: Batch Size vs. Prefix Homogeneity in LLM Inference
quote: SGLang's LPM and DFS-Weight incur scheduler overhead
proves: SGLang LPM and DFS-Weight batch formation took 46.62 s (31.2%) and 92.15 s (51.8%) of execution time in their test; moderately small prefix-homogeneous batches can beat larger heterogeneous ones; Feather scheduler 2-10x throughput over existing schedulers.
does_not_prove: Datacenter GPU setting; the 128-request FCFS fallback claimed by a search snippet was not found on the page I read.
bearing: threatens: prefix-homogeneous batching; supports: scheduler CPU cost of cache-aware ordering is a real cost on CPU-weak setups

title: Locality-aware Fair Scheduling in LLM Serving (DLPM)
quote: maintaining high throughput (up to 2.87$\times$ higher than VTC)
proves: Longest-prefix-match scheduling can starve clients; deficit-based DLPM keeps locality with fairness: up to 2.87x throughput over VTC and up to 7.18x lower per-client latency than distributed serving SOTA.
does_not_prove: Multi-tenant fairness focus; single-user Mac serving has no tenants.
bearing: threatens: fairness-aware prefix scheduling

title: Preble: Efficient Distributed Prompt Scheduling for LLM Serving
quote: 85% to 97% tokens in a prompt are shared with other prompts.
proves: Workload study of five prompt-heavy workloads: 85-97% of prompt tokens shared, each shared sequence reused by 8.6-126 requests; E2 routing exploits (route to longest-match GPU) when saved recompute exceeds new compute, else explores by load; 1.5x-14.5x avg and 2x-10x p99 latency over SOTA.
does_not_prove: Multi-GPU routing; workloads chosen for sharing (tool use, agents, QA), so share ratio is an upper bound.
bearing: threatens: cache-aware routing; supports: single-node only scheduling/eviction is the relevant scope for a Mac

title: CacheRoute: Planned Prefix-Affinity Routing for Large-Scale LLM Serving
quote: When affinity recovers too little KV work, its residual load skew reduces or erases the improvement.
proves: Planned prefix-affinity routing raises served KV hit rate from 64.1% to 93.2% and gives 176 QPS at 3.5 s p99 on 60 H100 (2.3x best of five baselines); but two 32B workloads are counterexamples where affinity gain vanishes, so authors recommend shadow replay before enabling.
does_not_prove: Cluster routing only.
bearing: negative result: cache affinity can lose when reusable work is small; threatens: cache-aware routing as novel

title: qwen-bailian-usagetraces-anon (GitHub)
quote: a two-hour sampled anonymized KVCache trace of requests sent to a single Qwen model serving cluster

title: vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py (main)
quote: preempted_req = self.running[-1]
proves: Victim selection: FCFS policy preempts the last request in the running list (most recently admitted); PRIORITY policy preempts max (priority, arrival_time). _preempt_request frees the request's blocks, sets num_computed_tokens = 0 and prepends it to the waiting queue; freed blocks go to the prefix-cache free queue, so the recompute can hit its own cached blocks if not yet evicted.
does_not_prove: Code shows mechanism, not why LIFO victim choice was picked; no victim-selection policy based on KV size, progress, or re-hit probability.
bearing: supports: victim selection by KV size/prefix re-hit likelihood (unexplored in vLLM)

title: vLLM docs: Quantized KV Cache
quote: Per-attention-head quantization is currently available only with the Flash Attention backend
proves: Upstream vLLM ships fp8_e4m3 / fp8_e5m2 KV cache on CUDA/ROCm with per-tensor or per-head scales (scales default to 1.0 without calibration); no int4/int8 KV listed; sliding-window layers are more sensitive.
does_not_prove: Gives no memory or throughput numbers; quantization is the only compression mechanism listed (no eviction, no sparse attention for dense models).
bearing: supports: only fp8 quantization ships in vLLM; eviction/low-rank remain out of tree

title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
quote: the key cache should be quantized per-channel.
proves: Keys per-channel, values per-token, 2-bit: 2.6x less peak memory, up to 4x larger batch, 2.35-3.47x throughput on their workload.
does_not_prove: Throughput measured in authors' HF-based stack, not a paged engine (D1 finds KIVI gains shrink and outputs lengthen 1.69x).
bearing: supports: asymmetric K/V bit allocation; threatens: novelty of plain K/V asymmetric quantization

title: KVQuant: Towards 10 Million Context Length LLM Inference with KV Cache Quantization
quote: < 0.1 perplexity degradation with 3-bit quantization on both Wikitext-2 and C4
proves: 3-bit KV with <0.1 PPL loss; LLaMA-7B at 1M context on one A100-80GB; custom kernels up to ~1.7x vs fp16 matrix-vector.
does_not_prove: Kernel-level speedups only; perplexity not task accuracy; no continuous batching or paged layout.
bearing: threatens: sub-4-bit KV quantization as novel

title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
quote: Our implementation of H$_2$O with 20% heavy hitters improves the throughput over three leading inference systems
proves: Accumulated-attention eviction keeping 20% heavy hitters; up to 29x/29x/3x throughput vs DeepSpeed Zero-Inference, HF Accelerate, FlexGen.
does_not_prove: Baselines are offloading systems, not vLLM-class paged engines; needs attention scores that FlashAttention does not return (D18).
bearing: threatens: score-based eviction novelty; supports: score-free eviction for fused kernels

title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
quote: SnapKV can process up to 380K context tokens on a single A100-80GB GPU
proves: Prompt-end observation window picks KV to keep; 3.6x generation speed and 8.2x memory efficiency at 16K inputs.
does_not_prove: HF implementation; selection is query-dependent and fails on later queries over the same context (D2: multi-request 15.2 vs 37.2).
bearing: threatens: one-shot prompt compression with prefix reuse

title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
quote: keeping the KV of initial tokens will largely recover the performance of window attention
proves: Sink tokens plus a recent window give stable LM up to 4M tokens and 22.2x over sliding-window recomputation.
does_not_prove: Stability is perplexity, not retrieval; D2 shows multi-turn collapse; TRT-LLM's sink_token_length is now deprecated (D25).
bearing: supports: window+sink as cheap baseline; threatens: windowed cache novelty

title: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling
quote: PyramidKV matches the performance of models with a full KV cache while retaining only 12% of the KV cache.
proves: Layer-wise budgets (more in low layers) keep LongBench parity at 12% of KV.
does_not_prove: Accuracy only; per-layer variable budgets fragment paged memory (D19); multi-request collapse (D2: 15.3).
bearing: threatens: per-layer budget allocation novelty

title: Palu: Compressing KV-Cache with Low-Rank Projection
quote: Palu compresses KV-Cache by 50% while maintaining strong accuracy
proves: Low-rank cached latents reconstructed on the fly; up to 1.89x on RoPE attention module, 2.91x with quantization.
does_not_prove: Module-level speedup only; no paged-engine or batched serving numbers; reconstruction cost not quantified in abstract.
bearing: supports: low-rank KV in a real engine as unstudied

title: MiniCache: KV Cache Compression in Depth Dimension for Large Language Models
quote: achieves a remarkable compression ratio of up to 5.02x
proves: Cross-layer merging of similar adjacent-layer KV: up to 5.02x compression and ~5x throughput on LLaMA-2-7B ShareGPT with 4-bit.
does_not_prove: Not in any shipping engine seen; interaction with paged blocks and prefix sharing untested.
bearing: supports: cross-layer sharing inside paged allocator as gap

title: Quest: Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: Quest keeps track of the minimal and maximal Key values in KV cache pages.
proves: Page-level min/max key metadata picks top pages per query; up to 2.23x self-attention speedup, 7.03x inference latency reduction.
does_not_prove: Batch-1 style evaluation; keeps full KV in memory (no capacity win); D2 shows multi-request accuracy drop 28.2 to 16.2.
bearing: supports: page-granular sparsity matches paged blocks; threatens: page-summary top-k novelty

title: MagicPIG: LSH Sampling for Efficient LLM Generation
quote: TopK attention itself suffers from quality degradation in certain downstream tasks
proves: LSH sampling with CPU-resident hash tables and attention; up to 5x decode throughput; 54 ms/token at 96K on RTX 4090.
does_not_prove: Relies on discrete GPU+CPU split; unified-memory Macs remove the PCIe premise; not in any upstream engine.
bearing: threatens: naive top-k sparse attention; supports: rethinking offload designs for unified memory

title: ShadowKV: KV Cache in Shadows for High-Throughput Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: support up to 6$\times$ larger batch sizes
proves: Low-rank key cache plus offloaded values; up to 6x batch and 3.04x throughput on A100.
does_not_prove: Custom system, not vLLM/SGLang; CPU offload premise; no prefix sharing.
bearing: supports: low-rank K + sparse V as building block

title: RetroInfer: A Vector Storage Engine for Scalable Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: up to 4.4X decoding throughput over full attention at 120K context
proves: RetrievalAttention successor: wave index + GPU-CPU wave buffer; 4.4x over full attention at 120K, 12.2x over sparse baselines at 1M.
does_not_prove: Long single contexts on discrete GPUs; short-context batched serving and reuse not the target.
bearing: threatens: retrieval-attention-as-index ideas at long context

title: [RFC]: Support sparse KV cache framework (vllm-project/vllm #5751)
quote: Add the corresponding logic for updating block table mapping and manage the related allocated/free blocks
proves: General partial-eviction RFC for vLLM opened June 2024; still open with keep-open label; never merged; no maintainer verdict on block manager or prefix caching fit.
does_not_prove: Says nothing about why it stalled; targets v1 block manager that later changed.
bearing: supports: eviction absent from upstream vLLM after 2+ years

title: PagedEviction: Structured Block-wise KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Large Language Model Inference
quote: FlashAttention never returns the attention score during the inference process.
proves: Score-based eviction cannot run inside PagedAttention; block-wise eviction on vLLM 0.9.0 with no kernel changes gives ~37% throughput over full cache at budget 1024 (LLaMA-3.2-1B), ~10-12% lower TPOT, up to 3.1x in page-size ablation.
does_not_prove: Synthetic 1024-in/8192-out workload; no prefix caching or multi-turn; A100 only.
bearing: threatens: block-granular eviction in vLLM; supports: block-size vs eviction granularity tradeoff

title: KV-Compress: Paged KV-Cache Compression with Variable Compression Rates per Attention Head
quote: evicts contiguous KV blocks within a PagedAttention framework
proves: Variable per-head eviction fragments paged memory so savings vanish unless blocks are evicted contiguously; vLLM integration up to 5.18x throughput via larger batches.
does_not_prove: Fork, not upstream; no prefix caching or multi-turn accuracy.
bearing: threatens: per-head eviction in vLLM; supports: fragmentation as the core system problem

title: vToken: Token-Level Virtualization for Reclaimable KV Caches
quote: This mismatch causes intra-block fragmentation, leaving a large fraction of allocated KV memory unreclaimable.
proves: Token eviction inside fixed-size blocks leaves memory unreclaimable; vToken in vLLM cuts retained blocks 27.2-72.3% vs naive evict, up to 1.37x SLA throughput, up to 2x concurrency.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not cover prefix caching (search snippet said shared-prefix blocks are excluded, unverified); CUDA only.
bearing: threatens: eviction-reclaim layers in vLLM (very recent, Aug 2026)

title: Zipage: Maintain High Request Concurrency for LLM Reasoning through Compressed PagedAttention
quote: We propose a comprehensive scheduling strategy and support prefix caching and asynchronous compression for Compressed PagedAttention.
proves: Token eviction combined with PagedAttention plus prefix caching and async compression; ~95% of full-KV accuracy at >2.1x speedup on math reasoning.
does_not_prove: Own engine; reasoning workloads only; how shared prefixes are kept intact is not in the abstract.
bearing: threatens: eviction+prefix-caching co-design for reasoning

title: SGLang docs: HiSparse: Hierarchical Sparse Attention
quote: HiSparse currently requires PD disaggregation mode.
proves: SGLang ships top-k sparse decode with a small GPU hot buffer and full KV in host memory, but only for trained-sparse models (DeepSeek Sparse Attention, DeepSeek V4, MiniMax M3), decode instance only.
does_not_prove: Does not apply post-hoc sparsity to dense models like Qwen3; no numbers on page.
bearing: supports: shipped sparse attention is architecture-trained, not post-hoc; post-hoc sparsity remains research-only

title: SGLang docs: Quantized KV Cache
quote: Currently, only per-tensor (scalar) scaling factors are supported.
proves: SGLang ships fp8_e5m2/fp8_e4m3 KV (per-tensor scales, default 1.0) and experimental nvfp4/fp4_mx; without fused dequant performance can be extremely slow; NVFP4 path excludes speculative decoding, PD disaggregation, hierarchical KV cache, LMCache.
does_not_prove: No throughput numbers; CUDA only.
bearing: supports: quantized KV vs spec decode / hierarchical cache interaction as open

title: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp in vLLM: Fine-Grained Sparse Attention in Action
quote: DSA's lightning indexer along with sparse attention presents challenges in continuous batching and paged attention.
proves: vLLM's only shipped sparse attention is model-native DSA: separate indexer K cache buffers, per-block (non-contiguous) indexer layout, separate prefill/decode indexer paths, fp8 MLA cache 656 bytes/token.
does_not_prove: Says nothing about prefix caching; post-hoc sparse methods for dense models not covered.
bearing: supports: trained-sparsity is the shipped path; threatens: claims that sparse attention is absent from engines

title: TensorRT-LLM KvCacheConfig reference

proves: TRT-LLM ships KV dtype fp8 / fp8_ds_mla / nvfp4, block reuse, and per-layer max_attention_window; sink_token_length is a deprecated field; no eviction or sparse-attention fields.
does_not_prove: Does not document how windows interact with block reuse or quantized KV.

title: GraniKV: Asymmetric Granularity KV-Cache Paging for Multi-Agent Systems with Long Shared Prefix

M6 24 GB with a 22 GB neighbour: suspensions 2 to 0 (148,830 replayed tokens avoided), fifth cold request 163.4 s to 45.6 s.
